crossStoryFindings: Stories 3-5 are coherent once canonical archive rows already exist: archive reads, turn derivation, and derived views share stable IDs and degradation semantics.

The seam between Story 2 finalization and Story 1 persistence is where the epic breaks: live execution output is still funneled through legacy `processHistoryItems`, so later stories rely on archive row shapes that the shipped runtime cannot actually produce.
Story 6 provenance enrichment and Story 5 tool-aware turn/view behavior are both validated mostly against hand-seeded archive rows rather than rows emitted by the real completion hooks.
architectureFindings: The Convex storage layer matches the tech design, but the control-plane finalization boundary never moved up to finalized runtime objects; it is still coupled to presentation-oriented `ProcessHistoryItem` records.
Read-time enrichment is correctly separated from canonical truth, but no upstream writer populates the related artifact/source IDs that the enrichment layer consumes.
Derived turns and derived views remain rebuildable projections and do not mutate archive truth; the main architectural drift is at capture time, not projection time.
epicCoverageAssessment: Both requested gates passed on May 5, 2026: `corepack pnpm run green-verify` and `corepack pnpm run verify-all`.
Coverage is strong for storage, ordering, pagination, turn grouping, derived-view refresh, and degraded-read behavior once archive rows already exist.

Coverage is weak on end-to-end emission: tests create `tool_call`, `tool_result`, and provenance-bearing archive rows directly in fixtures/service stores instead of proving that the live runtime can emit them.
`verify-all` still ends with a scaffold-only `test:e2e` step, so no browser-level end-to-end archive flow currently executes.
productionPathFindings: The default runtime path is still the shared placeholder execution payload in `apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/script-execution.service.ts`, and that payload emits a synthetic `process_event` plus placeholder side-work text instead of a real process-type model/tool/runtime flow.

Production archive append is currently limited to accepted user responses and legacy history-item bridging; there is no real append path for `reasoning`, `script_emission`, `tool_call`, or `tool_result` entries.
Artifact/source provenance enrichment is real on read, but no live writer currently persists the related artifact-version or source-provenance IDs that the read path expects.

blockingFindings.title: The shipped archive pipeline cannot emit four of the seven required canonical entry kinds
blockingFindings.evidence: `ExecutionResult` only carries legacy `ProcessHistoryItem[]` (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/provider-adapter.ts`), `processHistoryItemKindSchema` only allows `user_message`, `process_message`, `progress_update`, `attention_request`, `side_work_update`, and `process_event` (`apps/platform/shared/contracts/process-work-surface.ts`), and the archive compatibility bridge maps only `user_message`, `process_message`, and `process_event` into canonical rows (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/process-history-compat.service.ts`). `ProcessEnvironmentService` archives runtime output only through that bridge (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/process-environment.service.ts`), so the live system has no real append path for `reasoning`, `script_emission`, `tool_call`, or `tool_result`.

blockingFindings.title: Live archive writes never attach artifact-version or source-provenance references
blockingFindings.evidence: The read path is built to enrich `relatedArtifactVersionId` and `relatedSourceProvenanceId` (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/archive-read.service.ts`), but the shipped producers hard-code both fields to `null` (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/process-response.service.ts`, `apps/platform/server/services/archive/process-history-compat.service.ts`). The only execution-bridge payload is `ProcessHistoryItem`, which exposes `relatedArtifactId` but no artifact-version or source-provenance field (`apps/platform/shared/contracts/process-work-surface.ts`), so real archive rows cannot satisfy provenance visibility requirements. The passing provenance tests seed those IDs directly in fixtures and test stores (`tests/service/server/archive-api.test.ts`, `tests/fixtures/archive.ts`) instead of proving a live producer can emit them.

nonBlockingFindings.title: The default execution lane is still a placeholder path
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: `apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/script-execution.service.ts` still builds the repo-wide "default execution payload," writes a "Default Execution Summary," and reports "Execution placeholder completed..." while emitting only a single `process_event`. That is a material non-real production path for this epic because the archive is being exercised primarily against placeholder runtime output rather than real process-type execution.

unresolvedItems: A new finalized runtime-object contract is still needed if the archive is supposed to capture `reasoning`, `script_emission`, `tool_call`, and `tool_result` without collapsing back to presentation history rows.
The implementation still needs a concrete producer for `relatedArtifactVersionId` and `relatedSourceProvenanceId` during finalization; the current codebase only implements the read-side enrichment.
No executable end-to-end archive/browser suite currently runs because `test:e2e` is scaffold-only in the epic gate.
